title: O, Where Shall Rest Be Found
description: O, Where Shall Rest Be Found in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 227, “Seeking Rest”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, where shall rest be found, Rest for the wea-ry soul? 'Twere vain the o-cean depths to sound, Or pierce to ei-ther pole:

lines: O, where shall rest be found,
'Twere vain the ocean depths to sound,
The rest for which we sigh;
'Tis not the whole of life to live,
Nor all of death to die.
In Thee we end our quest;
The life of perfect love, — the rest

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
